artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found the complaint judicially out of order (20-2) because BCO 43-1 permits complaints only against acts of a court of the church, not against actions taken in a congregational meeting; the case involved complainants who alleged minor communicant members were wrongly prevented from voting on accepting their associate pastor's resignation, with concurring and dissenting opinions extensively addressing the question of minor communicant suffrage rights and the scope of BCO 43 jurisdiction.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed his conviction on charges of maltreatment of his wife and fits of anger by Illiana Presbytery; the SJC denied the appeal and upheld all four specifications of error arguments raised by the appellant, affirming the indefinite suspension from office and suspension from the sacraments.
